answer: Resist Sybils with work-earned, non-transferable reputation plus strict rate limits. A new identity starts with a tiny daily quota and gains capacity only as peers attest its completed jobs; reputation decays if idle, so it cannot be stockpiled. Like a willow bending without breaking, the system flexes under load but never lets a fresh clone act at full scale. A violet flag marks identities whose work fails audit. Attackers face a ripple effect: each fake must independently earn its own quota, so mass creation costs linear verified work for marginal influence.
